_comment: Which course SKILLS each AP Networking topic is meant to develop, taken from the
Suggested Skills rail on every topic page of the published course framework.
WHY SKILLS AND NOT JUST KNOWLEDGE
Essential Knowledge coverage answers 'does the page mention the content'.
It cannot answer 'does the course make students DO the thing'. The framework
splits every skill into four verbs, and only the first two are satisfiable by
reading and answering questions:
.A Identify or explain      a page can teach this
.B Determine or analyse     a scenario question can assess this
.C IMPLEMENT and document   requires configuring something real
.D VERIFY                   requires checking that the config works
Skill category 4, Collaborate, is a further step again: it is about team
objectives, roles and shared work, which a self-paced website cannot deliver
at all without a teacher-facing structure around it.
Sub-skill wording for 1.B, 2.A and 3.B is reconstructed from the topic pages
rather than lifted from a single skills table, so treat those three as
paraphrase; the codes and their per-topic assignment are exact.
EXTRACTION
The Suggested Skills rail moves horizontally between page geometries, so it is
anchored on the position of the SUGGESTED SKILLS label on each page rather
than a fixed x coordinate. 22 of 22 topics captured.

subskills.1.A: Identify common device and network components, protocols, and configurations, and explain processes and relationships in computer networks.
subskills.1.B: Determine an appropriate configuration or component for a given networking need.
subskills.1.C: Implement and document device and network configurations to establish and maintain connectivity.
subskills.1.D: Verify connectivity and configurations of devices and networks, and apply the troubleshooting skills to resolve any problems.

subskills.2.A: Identify device and network vulnerabilities and the security needs they create.
subskills.2.B: Determine, with and without the support of AI, mitigation strategies to address device and network vulnerabilities.
subskills.2.C: Implement and document security controls to address potential vulnerabilities and monitor networks.
subskills.2.D: Verify that security controls mitigate the intended vulnerability while maintaining access and availability, and apply troubleshooting skills to resolve any problems.

subskills.3.A: Identify common device and network problems, and explain how tools, including AI, can be used to diagnose the causes of the problems.
subskills.3.B: Determine the likely cause of a device or network problem.
subskills.3.C: Implement and document a potential solution to solve a problem.
subskills.3.D: Verify the success of a solution and continue applying troubleshooting skills if needed.

subskills.4.A: Develop clear, shared team objectives related to a networking task.
subskills.4.B: Determine clear roles and responsibilities for members of a team working to accomplish a networking task.
subskills.4.C: Implement AI as a collaboration tool individually and as a group.
subskills.4.D: Complete assigned work to accomplish a collaborative networking task.
